Dated this the 8th day of January, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.256/2010 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Perumbavoor is the appellant herein.

The respondents in the O.P.
are the respondents herein.

The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 3.1.2010.
2.

According to the petitioner, on 3.1.2010 at about 9.30 a.m., while he was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-17C-2173, a jeep bearing registration No.KL7H-7072 came from opposite direction and hit against the motor cycle and as a result of which, he sustained serious injuries.
The 1 st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the jeep KL7H-7072.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
3. The 1st and 2nd respondents remained ex-parte.
The 3rd 2025:KER:3249 respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle.
4. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exhibits A1 to A16, Exhibit B1 and Exhibit C1.

sentences.text: 5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.8,58,497/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

8. Heard Sri. Aju Mathew, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Smt. S. Jayasree,
learned Standing Counsel for the 3 rd respondent.
9.
The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.

Though in the written statement the 3rd respondent has 2025:KER:3249 contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motor cycle, at the time of arguments such a contention was not taken.
The petitioner has produced Exhibit A3, copy of the Final Report involved in the crime registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, in respect to the above accident.
In the light of the above Final Report, negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle stands proved.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent, being the insurer, is liable to indemnify the compensation, which is liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.
10. The petitioner was aged 49 years on the date of the accident, on 3.1.2010.
According to the petitioner, he was a businessman earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
The Tribunal fixed his income at Rs.5,000/- as he could not prove the income claimed in the OP.

However, as per dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], even the notional income of a Coolie during the year 2010 will come to Rs.7,500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstance, the notional income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed at Rs.7,500/-.
11. In the accident, the petitioner sustained very serious injuries.

As 2025:KER:3249 per Exhibit C1-disability certificate issued by the medical board, Government Medical College Hospital,
Kottayam, his permanent physical disability was fixed at 70%.

As per Exhibit A9 wound certificate issued from the Medical Trust Hospital, Ernakulam, the petitioner sustained fracture of fibular head, contusion on the corpus callosal, fracture right 6 th and 7th ribs, fracture right clavicle,
fracture radius right forearm, fracture fibula head of right knee.

He was treated as in-patient in the said hospital from 3.1.2010 to 27.1.2010.
12.

Since, on the date of accident, he was aged 49 years, 25% of his income is to be added towards future prospects, and the multiplier to be applied is 13, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. In the above circumstances, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.10,23,750/-.

3 14.
Towards loss of earnings, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/- being his monthly income for a period of six months.

The leaned counsel for the petitioner would argue that because of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the disability on account of those injuries, he lost income for a considerable period and therefore, he prayed for enhancement of 2025:KER:3249 compensation on that head.

Considering the fact that the petitioner sustained very serious injuries including several fractures and suffered 70% permanent physical disability, I hold that towards loss of earnings,
monthly income for a period of nine months will be a reasonable one.
Therefore, towards loss of earnings a sum of Rs.67,500/- (7500x9) is awarded.
15. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/- and towards loss of amenities a sum of Rs. 35,000/- was awarded.
The learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that the compensation awarded on those heads are too meager when compared to the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

Considering the fact that the petitioner sustained very serious injuries including several fractures and suffered 70% permanent physical disability, the compensation towards the heads 'pain and suffering' and loss of amenities are on the lesser side.

Therefore, the compensation towards pain and suffering is enhanced to Rs.3,00,000/-, and compensation on the head loss of amenities is enhanced to Rs.2,00,000/-.
16.

Towards extra nourishment, the tribunal has awarded Rs.1,500/-, which, according to the petitioner is too meager when compared to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the disability suffered by him on 2025:KER:3249 account of those injuries.

Therefore, compensation for extra nourishment is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.
17.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

18. Therefore, the petitioner/appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.18,07,247/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
Sl. Head of claim Amount awarded The amount given in No. by the appeal (Rs.)
Tribunal(Rs) 1 Loss of earnings 30,000/- 67,500/- 2 Transport to hospital 1,500/-
1,500/- 3 Extra nourishment 1,500/- 20,000/- 4 Damage to clothes 1,000/- 1,000/-
5
Medical expenses 1,87,497/- 1,87,497/- 6 Pain and suffering 50,000/- 3,00,000/- 7 Loss of amenities 35,000/- 2,00,000/- 8

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3 rd respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.18,07,247 /- (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs Seven Thousand Two Hundred and Forty Seven Only), less the amount 2025:KER:3249 already deposited, if any, from the date of the petition till realisation, with interest @9% per annum, excluding interest for a period of 46 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
(The enhanced amount of compensation will carry interest at the rate of 8% per annum alone).
